disposition_reason: Antibacterial MICs of bismuth(III) for aquaculture pathogens (13 to >780 µM) and an injected bismuth treatment trial in sole; no tissue residues measured.

study.design: in vitro susceptibility testing and fish infection-treatment trial
study.method: Broth microdilution MIC; intraperitoneal treatment trial with Kaplan-Meier survival

regulatory_or_exposure: Fish treatment doses: 0.1 mL of 1.3 µM or 13 µM bismuth-deferiprone by intraperitoneal injection; 65 µM in uninfected controls (pp. 5 to 6).
non_numeric_findings: Bismuth MICs ranged from 13 to more than 780 µM across aquaculture pathogens (Table 1).
Authors propose bismuth therapy to reduce antibiotic use in aquaculture (abstract).
